sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: who belongs where across four near-identical numbered lists and one proposal with none (hook h32, sketch i04). Target medium (user 2026-10-10: "there is no slot for Easy Tier for this bundle, we should target medium and high"; same day: "after checking difficulty, it blocks easy tier. So we must target at medium or hard."). Rev 0 measured "In band — Medium tier" (Low 0/5, Medium 3/5, Version 94672c) and was submitted. Rev 1 answers the reviewer's "Revision requested" of 2026-10-12 and needs a new difficulty result, because the necessary documents changed.
- Revision 2 scope (2026-10-13): one repair for the Run 2 result on rev 1 ("Between levels", Low 0/5, Medium 4/5; the page: "Make it a little harder, so the medium model reaches your answer only some of the time"). The question gains a second, parallel count, "and how many in all five?", gold 12, so the answer is "10, 12". Everything rev 1 did for the reviewer stays: Docs 3 and 4 ticked with the exclusion role, the added quotes, Steps 2, 4, 6 and 7 as reworded. Steps 8 and 9, component c2 and nine evidence rows are new; the reviewer notes and the failure-mode reason now name both counts. Why this repair and no other: over the two runs on this wording (one solver task, since only the ticks differed) the medium model was right 7 times in 10. Of the six right attempts whose text was recorded, five never mention the more prescriptive list (Run 1 Medium 1, 3, 5; Run 2 Medium 1, 3) and one does (Run 2 Medium 2); they count inside the first list and stop. Run 2 Medium 4 read only the second list and answered none. So which lists make up the rule's all-unit amendments is a step the medium model does not reliably take, and the first count never needed it. The second count needs it: EPA says of both lists that they "apply to all CCR units" (D03 L246 and L278). Not done: the Coach's suggestion to define the term in the question (it names both lists and would hand over that step; its "Why" also misreads the low attempts, which failed on Wyoming and Wisconsin, not on reading one list); a wording-only edit (it would re-measure the same task).
- Revision 1 scope (2026-10-12): only what the reviewer asked. (1) Docs 3 and 4 ticked as "Exclusion / condition source", with the reviewer note. (2) Evidence added: from Doc 3 and Doc 4 the approving sentence and the entries for 257.50(c), "Infiltration" and "Liquids"; the "did not adopt these amendments and did not seek approval of these provisions" sentence from Docs 3, 4, 5 and 6; Alabama's not-approved entries 1, 4 and 5. (3) Reasoning: Step 2 says "3 of the 5 entries"; Step 4 cites Docs 3-6 as sources and no longer says they are not needed; Step 6 says "each lacks an approved version only in Wyoming and Wisconsin"; Step 7 states which amendments are excluded (missing in one State, missing in three). Question, answer, component, tags and failure modes are unchanged; the reviewer wrote "The gold answer (10) is correct and both traps land".
- Dependency plan: Doc 2 L280-L282 Wyoming seeks approval of no Legacy Rule amendment -> Wyoming lacks every one. Doc 5 L308-L329 Alabama's approved list, 17 entries; L337-L343 five entries not approved, three of them the added all-unit definitions. Doc 6 L309-L320 Wisconsin's approved list, 11 entries, two of them ("Infiltration", "Liquids") among Alabama's unapproved three. Docs 3 and 4 L246-L272 / L316-L338 approve all twenty, so no third State lacks any. Common entries 11 - 2 = 9; Alabama-only 17 - 9 = 8 (missing in Wyoming and Wisconsin); Wisconsin-only 2 (missing in Wyoming and Alabama); 8 + 2 = 10.
- Universe: the twenty entries of the all-unit list in D03 L247-L272 and D04 L317-L338 (identical). By number of approving States (script over the extracted entries, 2026-10-10): four States (Virginia, Louisiana, Alabama, Wisconsin), 9: the "website" wording, 257.52, "Active facility", "CCR landfill", "State director", 257.61(a), 257.80(a), 257.90(a), 257.104(a). Three States, 10: with Alabama but not Wisconsin, 257.50(c), 257.51, "CCR surface impoundment", "CCR unit", "Inactive CCR surface impoundment", "Technically feasible", "Technically infeasible", 257.100(a)(1); with Wisconsin but not Alabama, "Infiltration", "Liquids". Two States (Virginia, Louisiana), 1: "Contains both CCR and liquids". Wyoming approves none, so the numbers of States lacking a version are 1, 2 and 3 for those groups. The twelve more prescriptive all-unit amendments (D03 L278-L290, D04 L348-L360, D05 L344-L356, D06 L404-L417) are approved nowhere and lack a version in all five States.
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only source of Wyoming's position (grep "Amendments made in the Legacy": D02 L282 only); without it the answer is 1. Doc 5 is the only source of Alabama's seventeen and its unapproved definitions; Doc 6 of Wisconsin's eleven (9 and 3 without them, Document check on rev 0). Docs 3 and 4 are condition sources: each is the only document showing that its State approves all twenty, which is what rules that State out as a third one lacking a version. The Document check on rev 0 did not test them; a solver working from the other four proposals would still reach 10, so the platform's check may call them "not needed", and the form's reviewer note is the stated route for that case. The reviewer asked for this role in terms (notes/feedback-q02.md).
- Selected-lever checks: Who belongs where: the same numbered entries recur in four proposals with different membership. Match, then exclude: decoys are "Contains both CCR and liquids" (lacking in three States) and the nine entries lacking in Wyoming alone. Scatter the pieces: Wyoming's single grouped item is itemised only in the other proposals.
- Targeted failure modes: unchanged in rev 1 at the reviewer's word ("both traps land"). Mode 1 (Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list): Wyoming left out of the lacking States leaves only "Contains both CCR and liquids" missing in exactly two States (Alabama, Wisconsin): 1. Mode 2 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope / Picks the wrong entity or section): "Infiltration" and "Liquids" read as approved for Alabama because Wisconsin's list approves them: 8. Measured on rev 0 (Run 1, routes read from the traces, notes/feedback-q02.md): every low attempt failed the Wyoming link and also read Wisconsin's list as approving all twenty (0, 0, 0, 0, "One"); both medium misses misread Alabama's list (as all twenty: 9; with the wrong three missing: 6).
- Calculation verification: python 2026-10-10 (caller) over the numbered entries extracted from text/D03-D06: Counter of approving States {4: 9, 3: 10, 2: 1}; lacking in exactly two of five = approved in exactly three = 10. By hand: 11 - 2 = 9; 17 - 9 = 8; 8 + 2 = 10. Rev 1 changes no figure. Alabama's not-approved list counted from text/D05 L338-L343: five entries.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 10, 9 or 8 as a count of amendments or compares two States' lists. The page overview names no list.
- Readings of the second count (reported, not cleared): (a) the all-unit amendments read as the first list only gives "10, 0"; the words against it are EPA's "apply to all CCR units and are more prescriptive" for the second list. (b) Read as the second list only gives "0, 12" (Run 2 Medium 4's reading); the words against it are "amended certain terms and provisions that apply to all CCR units" for the first. (c) Counting the paragraphs inside an entry instead of entries (four of the twelve say "these amendments") gives no settled number above 12; against it, the first count already takes one numbered entry as one amendment and every recorded attempt that listed the second group counted 12 (Run 1 high, Run 2 Medium 2 and 4). A reviewer could still raise (c). (d) 257.90(g), 257.95(h)(2) and the vegetative-cover provisions lack approval widely, and three low attempts counted them; they are not amendments made by the 2024 rule (D02 L282-L290 lists them apart from it).
- Precision/readings: an amendment is one numbered entry of EPA's lists; "Technically feasible" and "Technically infeasible" are separate entries, each called "this amendment", in every list that carries them. "lack an approved State version" follows EPA's split between "approving the State's version" and "not being approved"; an entry absent from Wisconsin's enumerated approved list has no approved Wisconsin version. "exactly two" excludes the entry missing in three States and those missing in one. Alabama's not-approved list also holds 257.71(d) and 257.90(g), which are not among the rule's all-unit amendments. Whole count, no rounding.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (intake: incomplete false, gap 0 for all six documents).
- Style/set review: 27 words, one ask, wording as measured. Sibling sketch i03 is closed. q01 (dropped) shares no fact.
- Warnings answered (rev 2): see the floor result recorded after the preflight below.
- Warnings answered (rev 1, historical): rev 1 floor 0 FAIL, 4 WARN (2026-10-12). origin: claude is the actual writer; the export sheet takes origin user only, reported as is. Two WARNs caution against the exclusion role for D03 and D04, and one notes five listed documents: all three follow the reviewer's own request ("Add Doc 3 (Virginia) and Doc 4 (Louisiana) as necessary documents, role 'Exclusion / condition source'"), and each note names what the document rules out, a third State lacking a version. No form-numbers line is predicted: Step 2's 17, 5, 3 and 2024 are printed near the start of Doc 5 (characters 9,171, 7,047, 7,376 and 14,804), Step 3's 11 near the start of Doc 6 (character 89), 2 near the start of every ticked document, Step 4 holds no digits, and 9, 8 and 10 are exact "=" results. sections.question: Under EPA's five proposed State coal-ash program approvals, how many of the 2024 Legacy Rule's all-unit amendments would lack an approved State version in exactly two States, and how many in all five? Give the two counts in that order.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, Wyoming Partial Program): Wyoming "is not seeking approval for" the "Amendments made in the Legacy CCR Surface Impoundments and CCR Management Units Final Rule", so no amendment made by that rule would have an approved Wyoming version. Wyoming is one of the States without one for every such amendment.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 5, Alabama Partial Program): for the terms and provisions that rule changed for all CCR units, "EPA is approving the State's version of these requirements", a numbered list that ends at entry 17. The next list, of amendments that "are not being approved", has 5 entries, and 3 of the 5 entries are 2024 Legacy Rule all-unit definitions: "Contains both CCR and liquids", "Infiltration" and "Liquids". The other two entries concern alternate liner demonstrations and suspension of groundwater monitoring.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 6, Wisconsin Partial Program): "EPA is approving the State's version of these requirements", a numbered list that ends at entry 11. It includes "Infiltration" and "Liquids", which Alabama's approved list does not; every other Wisconsin entry is also on Alabama's approved list.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 3, Doc 4, Doc 5 and Doc 6): Virginia's list ("EPA is approving the State's version of the following requirements") and Louisiana's ("EPA is approving the State's version of these requirements") carry every entry on Alabama's or Wisconsin's approved list, among them "Infiltration", "Liquids" and the scope provision on inactive impoundments that Wisconsin's list lacks, and "Contains both CCR and liquids" as well. Virginia and Louisiana therefore have an approved version of every one of them, which is why an amendment missing in Wyoming and one other State is missing in exactly two States. The rule's other all-unit amendments are the more prescriptive ones: each of these four proposals says the State "did not adopt these amendments and did not seek approval of these provisions", and Wyoming seeks approval of none, so they lack an approved version in all five States.
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): entries on both Alabama's and Wisconsin's approved lists, which are Wisconsin's entries less "Infiltration" and "Liquids": 11 - 2 = 9.
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): entries approved for Alabama but not for Wisconsin: 17 - 9 = 8. They are the scope provision on inactive impoundments, the reserved effective-date section, the definitions of "CCR surface impoundment", "CCR unit", "Inactive CCR surface impoundment", "Technically feasible" and "Technically infeasible", and the compliance-deadline provision for inactive impoundments. Virginia, Louisiana and Alabama approve them, so each lacks an approved version only in Wyoming and Wisconsin.
Step 7. First count (Doc 2, Doc 3, Doc 4, Doc 5 and Doc 6): "Infiltration" and "Liquids" are approved for Virginia, Louisiana and Wisconsin, so each lacks an approved version only in Wyoming and Alabama. Adding them: 8 + 2 = 10. Amendments missing in only one State are excluded: the entries on both Alabama's and Wisconsin's lists lack an approved version in Wyoming alone. The amendment missing in three States is excluded too: "Contains both CCR and liquids" lacks an approved version in Wyoming, Alabama and Wisconsin.
Step 8. Source input (Doc 3, Doc 4, Doc 5 and Doc 6): the more prescriptive amendments are the rule's other all-unit amendments, the ones that "apply to all CCR units and are more prescriptive than the requirements in the 2015 CCR Rule". They form a list that ends at entry 12 in Virginia's, Louisiana's and Alabama's proposals and runs from a to l in Wisconsin's, with the same entries in each, and each of these four States "did not adopt these amendments and did not seek approval of these provisions".
Step 9. Second count (Doc 2, Doc 3, Doc 4, Doc 5 and Doc 6): Wyoming seeks approval of no amendment made by the rule, so those 12 lack an approved State version in all five States. No entry of the first list does, because Virginia and Louisiana approve every one of them. The two counts, in the order asked, are 10 and 12.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 2 groups Wyoming's unapproved 2024 amendments; leaving Wyoming out gives 1 and 0. Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 6 approves "Infiltration" and "Liquids", which Doc 5 lists as not approved for Alabama; treating Alabama like Wisconsin gives 8 and 12. Gold: 10 and 12.
